Wednesday was a mixed-to-soft session for Jaleel's book, with the overall unrealized position sitting at −2.87%. The day's damage came from two concentrated hits: Expand Energy (EXE, 4.1% weight) cratered −5.83%, and Adobe (ADBE, 5.3% weight) fell −2.83%, the latter dragged by macro rotation fears — Middle East tensions and renewed inflation anxiety pushing traders out of growth names ahead of key economic data. Lululemon (LULU) also shed −2.43% and S&P Global (SPGI) −1.40%, adding quiet pressure. On the bright side, On Holding (ONON) gained +1.46%, NVIDIA (NVDA) added +0.82%, and Gilead (GILD) ticked up +0.94%, offering partial offsets across the book's largest positions.

The most uncomfortable drift remains LULU and BSX. Lululemon is down −24.9% in the book against a STRONG BUY verdict — a guidance-cut risk flag still active, with Americas comps negative for a fifth straight period and the next catalyst not until December 9. That's a wide gap between thesis and price with no near-term resolution. Boston Scientific (BSX, 8.9% weight) sits at −10.4% with a slashed growth outlook and management guiding flat through Q3; the Oct 28 earnings print will be the real test. RKLB carries an AVOID verdict at a −18.7% loss — that combination demands a hard look.

Watch ADBE closely: the narrative (AI-moat erosion, CFO exit, ARR de-emphasis) is doing more damage than the fundamentals justify after a beat-and-raise quarter, but narrative-driven selloffs can persist. EXE's single-session −5.83% move warrants understanding the catalyst — whether energy-sector specific or broader macro — before treating it as noise.
